main_issue: Whether and how Agent D can use the shared small room for about fifteen minutes of prayer daily, given the others' use of it at various times

A-B.evidence: A and B never address each other; both raise scheduling constraints (T3, T4) and both end up accepting D's check-in approach (T9, T12).

A-C.evidence: A and C never address each other; both have time conflicts (T1, T7) and both end up accepting D's flexible arrangement (T9, T18).

A-D.evidence: A said 4-5:30 is unpredictable (T3, T9) and asked D to find a gap outside the block; D agreed 'before 4 p.m. is fine with me' (T10).

B-C.evidence: B and C never address each other; both ultimately accept D's check-in approach (T12, T18).

B-D.evidence: B first only stated needing in-and-out access (T4, T6), then said D's check-in idea 'sounds better' (T12); D thanked B (T13).

C-D.evidence: C said 1 o'clock was a problem (T7); after D asked about flexibility, C offered 12-2 (T16); D proposed they check with each other (T17); C: 'that works for me' (T18).
